Two divisions through the Lower Peninsula were included, the eastern one included a route between Detroit and Toledo via Monroe.

evidence.quote: Some residents complained that it was a traffic hazard in the middle of an intersection. On June 20, 1923, the statue was moved to a new location in Soldiers and Sailors Park along the River Raisin.

evidence.claim: A paper mill occupied this battlefield before its recovery as parkland.
evidence.quote: The River Raisin Paper Company built a large paper mill on the site around 1911, which operated under multiple owners until 1995.

evidence.claim: The park preserves the site of the January 1813 Battle of Frenchtown in Michigan, fought during the War of 1812.
evidence.quote: The River Raisin National Battlefield Park preserves the location of the January 1813 Battle of Frenchtown in southeastern Michigan, and is the only national battlefield park marking a site of the War of 1812.

evidence.claim: British soldiers under Henry Procter and Indigenous warriors under Roundhead counterattacked American forces led by James Winchester.
evidence.quote: British soldiers led by Colonel Henry Procter and Indigenous warriors led by Roundhead mounted a counterattack against the American forces led by Brigadier General James Winchester

evidence.claim: After the mill closed in 1995, Monroe organized efforts to restore the site.
evidence.quote: Expansion to the present-day park boundaries commenced in 1995 with the closure of the paper mill, at which time the City of Monroe organized efforts to restore the entire battlefield site.

evidence.claim: The mill was demolished by 2009 and cleanup finished in 2010. National park operations began that October.
evidence.quote: the paper mill was demolished by 2009, the cleanup finished in 2010

evidence.claim: National park operations began that October.
evidence.quote: River Raisin National Battlefield Park officially began operation as a national park unit on October 22, 2010.

evidence.claim: Monroe’s numbered downtown streets began with Henry Disbrow’s 1817 grid, modeled on New York City’s system.
evidence.quote: The area dates back to 1817 when the first roads were drawn out on a piece of land given by local landowner Joseph Loranger for the establishment of the village for the newly organized Monroe County.  The grid plan, drawn up by Henry Disbrow, was modeled after the system used in New York City, with streets named after numbers.

evidence.claim: The land came from Joseph Loranger for a village serving the newly organized county.
evidence.quote: land given by local landowner Joseph Loranger for the establishment of the village for the newly organized Monroe County.

evidence.claim: The county government has occupied its courthouse plot since 1817, though the current courthouse dates to 1880.
evidence.quote: The current county courthouse was built in 1880, although the plot of land it is located on has housed the seat of the county government since 1817.
